summary: Solder production is finally online. After several days of preparation, the full chain is operational. For now, I’m storing output in a steel chest — my first one. It holds twenty stacks, a massive upgrade compared to the eight of iron and four of wood.

With solder running, I shifted focus back to expansion. I began preparing additional space for more fish turbines. The groundwork is in place, but the system isn’t fully connected yet. It will take more time before everything is brought online and contributing to the grid.

I made another trip out for fishing today, this time using a car. Navigating in complete darkness proved to be more dangerous than expected — visibility was near zero, and I collided with rocks multiple times before reaching the shore. The vehicle barely held together by the time I arrived.

The return trip was worse. A nearby biter nest launched an attack and destroyed the car entirely while I was away. I didn’t have enough materials on hand to rebuild it, but I did have just enough to assemble a chaingunner. I cleared the hostiles that destroyed the vehicle and used it to make the trip back to base. Not efficient, but effective.
Despite the disruption, progress continues. Fish turbine expansion is underway, solder production is stable, and the factory is steadily pushing into more advanced territory.

Research reached a plateau today. I completed Basic Mining Speed 5, Basic Reach 5, and Basic Crafting Speed 5 — effectively exhausting the current tier of quality-of-life upgrades. Future progress will now depend more on infrastructure than personal efficiency.
